gcc.role: reference: the matrix C baseline (gcc 14 -O2, the same gcc:14 image as languages/c)

clang-lp64.role: check: the lp64.sh-transformed source compiled natively; identical machine code except the printf format string, so it must count like the native column to within a few instructions

transforms: languages/wasm/c/lp64.sh on every wasm build: long -> long long, %ld/%lu/%li -> %lld/%llu/%lli, L/UL literal suffixes -> LL/ULL (wasm32 is ILP32)
asymmetries: wasi-sdk's clang 23.1.0 and the official LLVM 23.1.0 release are built from different commits of the same release
the native binary links glibc, the wasm module links wasi-libc (malloc: glibc ptmalloc vs wasi-libc dlmalloc)

vector code: native clang -O2 emits NEON vector instructions in main for sha256 (46 static), fannkuch (16), polymorphism (8), k-means (3), dijkstra and blur (1 each), none in gemm; the wasm build has no simd128 (wasi-sdk 34 default). Enabling -msimd128 moves only gemm, k-means, sha256 and fannkuch, by 0.6 to 6% (codegen experiment)

wasm32 is ILP32 even after lp64.sh: pointers and size_t are 32-bit, so pointer-holding structs (binary-trees' nodes) are smaller and every address is a 32-bit offset zero-extended into the 64-bit heap base

unchangedSourcesOnWasm32.how: canonical languages/c/<b>.c compiled with wasi-sdk 34 clang -O2 (no lp64.sh), run on wasmtime 50 at n1, output compared with spec.json
